purpose: Define the movement intent, contact rules, measurable targets, coaching cues, and compensation signals for a synthesized stationary left-forward split-stance lunge reference.

authorityBoundary.notes: Engineering reference for the shipped avatar. Human proportions, stance length, ankle mobility, and lunge style require later calibration.

stance.cue: Set the left foot forward and the right foot back on two stable rails rather than a tightrope.

coachCues: Start in a stable split stance with the left foot forward and right foot back.
Keep the whole front foot planted and the rear forefoot connected to the floor.
Lower the body mostly straight down between the feet instead of lunging the torso forward.
Let the front knee track in the same direction as the front foot.
Drop the rear knee toward the floor while keeping the pelvis controlled.
Push through the front whole foot and rear forefoot to rise back to the same split stance.

compensationSignals.meaning: front knee caves inward relative to front foot
stance becomes too narrow laterally for stable reference
pelvis drifts materially away from the split-stance support corridor
pelvis/torso travel forward dominates vertical descent
rear knee does not move toward the floor as the body lowers
front/rear knee-angle targets are not approached

sourceEvidenceBoundary: Crouched sneaking provides candidate split-stance/asymmetric leg-loading mechanics but is explicitly not treated as a canonical lunge clip. Squat/hinge evidence contributes grounded knee/hip flexion mechanics only.
